text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel continues to deny allegations he called Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer a "real pig" during the EU summit in Amsterdam, but says he will not take action for slander. Chancellor Viktor Klima is staying out of the affair.
- The trade union congress OeGB has refused proposals for pension reforms and strongly opposes a reduction of pensions.
- Base unemployment is on the rise. Four out of five jobless people will not be able to find jobs even in an economic upswing, the Institute for Higher Studies says.
- Civil servants in the finance ministry are planning to hold a demonstration on July 9 against pay cuts and staff reductions as a result of the government's austerity policies.
- The Chamber of Economy is against the government's plans to introduce road pricing for trucks and wants an amendment to the road financing law immediately.
- The number of trucks passing through the Alpine Brenner pass fell by 5.17 percent in 1996 which shows higher tariffs have had an impact.
DIE PRESSE
- Membership of Austria's trade union congress hit an all-time low in 1996 with 48,000 fewer members.
- Uncertainty for hospital patients in 1998. Health bills are to be replaced with chips but the funding for the new system remains open.
- The Vienna bourse reached a record high of 1,339.87 in the wake of international gains. A hike in U.S. interest rates could jeopardise chances of a further rally.

- A price war is seen on the mobile phone market which is expected to swell to one million phones by the end of the year. The planned auction of the third licence is turning into a farce with only one prospective bidder.
- The economy ministry fears further declines in tourism over the summer with the deficit in the summer season expected to hit eight billion schillings from one billion last year.
KURIER
- A new tobacco tax on cigarette imports from non-European Union countries came into effect on July 1 but is not seen deterring buyers.
- The cost of local phone calls will rise by up to 73 percent in November while long distance calls will be cheaper.
- The investment banks of Creditanstalt and Bank Austria will be merged retrospectively from January 1.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Europe is the most expensive place for companies in the world. Austria is ranked as the sixth most expensive while Germany has the highest labour costs.
